What is Indefinite pronouns have fixed agreement? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Indefinite pronouns have fixed agreement: each/every/everyone/someone/nobody are always singular; few/many/several are always plural; some/all/most agree with their of-phrase. 'Neither/either' are singular alone but follow the nearer subject in 'neither…nor' pairs.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Indefinite pronouns have fixed agreement?
questions.a: Students think 'everyone/everybody' is plural because it means 'all people' — semantic plurality — and write 'everyone are'.
